recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if OO later decides that the external/incubator SupplyRequest artifact should again be referenceable from core ServiceRequest.replaces, or if FHIR-54619's later alignment decision changes before publication.
issue_request: FHIR-50001 was an Applied OO change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking that ServiceRequest.replaces be able to reference RequestOrchestration for grouped-order replacement workflows. The resolution listed a broader request-target set including RequestOrchestration and SupplyRequest, with other changes deferred to separate JIRAs.
initial_application: Upstream commit 0fb7e5cd6bf2cbed816e1a9434c53e586590cccc, linked from Jira via PR #3532, added RequestOrchestration and related request targets to source/servicerequest/structuredefinition-ServiceRequest.xml for ServiceRequest.replaces.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini keeps ServiceRequest and RequestOrchestration in the active core build, but has no active SupplyRequest entry after commit 3b38b80cf23f9cbb306fab8fcedb293315478c32 removed several OO resources from core and pointed to the OO incubator. Later OO issue FHIR-54619 aligned ServiceRequest.basedOn and ServiceRequest.replaces to the current nine target profiles, including RequestOrchestration and excluding SupplyRequest.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative ServiceRequest StructureDefinition already includes RequestOrchestration on ServiceRequest.replaces, and the only remaining difference from the original resolution is explained by later build-scope and WG alignment decisions.

related_jiras.note: Later OO decision aligns ServiceRequest.basedOn and ServiceRequest.replaces to the current nine target profiles, confirming RequestOrchestration support and excluding SupplyRequest.
